The *Yūthikapupphiyattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative located in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. In the standard structure of the *Apadāna*, the text records the biographical verses and past meritorious deeds of an elder monk (*thera*), specifically associated with the offering of jasmine (*yūthikā*) flowers. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages, though no official English title is assigned [SuttaCentral].
No cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora meet the match threshold, but automated analysis reveals extensive Pali-internal text reuse [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus identifies 76 matching passages across 27 other Pali texts, pointing to the heavily formulaic nature of this genre of verse [DharmaNexus]. The most significant alignment is found in the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, first volume), sharing 23 matches totaling 2,190 characters, with an extended alignment between segments 2.4–4.3 of the *apadāna* and segments 1280–1284 of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. The work also shares substantial repetitive verse stock (especially segments 2.3–7.1) with numerous other flower-offering accounts in the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Kiṁkaṇikapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 201), *Gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 131), *Kiṅkaṇipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 205), and *Punnāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 161 and Tha-Ap 335) [DharmaNexus].
